correctness.rationale: The two-component A5 condition implies a line flex meets the cubic only once with multiplicity three. Enumerating line-pair incidences forces (a,b,c)=(4,3,0), impossible with only two nonflex lines, or (5,0,0), impossible by parity on six lines. For two cubics and three lines, no nodes forces concurrency, the second triple is both cubics with one line, and cubic-cubic Bézout gives impossible 9=1+3s. All component and branch cases are exhausted.

value.rationale: The result resolves three specifically recorded degree-nine geometric realizability gaps in cubic–line arrangement theory, leaving only one of six numerically admissible cases potentially free. It combines saturated flex tangencies, line-arrangement parity and cubic-cubic intersection congruences and is independent of computational Jacobian conjectures.
